_meta.status: ACTIVE — this file names the release actor. It names no code owner, on purpose.
_meta.purpose: The identities governance depends on. Today that is one thing: which actor may create a production release tag. Reviewer identity is deferred, explicitly, below.
_meta.why_the_release_actor_is_an_app: GitHub identifies ruleset bypass actors numerically, and the actor types it accepts are Integration, OrganizationAdmin, RepositoryRole and Team. There is no User. A person cannot be granted release authority on a repository ruleset at all — so 'the owner cuts releases' is not expressible, and writing the owner's user id under any of those types would be a false statement that the local validator cannot detect and GitHub rejects later. A dedicated App is the only encoding that is both accepted and true.
_meta.app_id_is_not_the_installation_id: actor_id below is the GitHub App ID — the number on the App's settings page. It is NOT the installation ID, which is a different number, appears in the /settings/installations/<id> URL, and identifies this repository's install of the App rather than the App itself. A ruleset is already repository-scoped; an installation id there would be both redundant and wrong. Neither is the repository owner's user id, 36742102, which is what N-1's read-only verification refused.
what_this_file_cannot_establish: that App 4902397 exists, or that the id is one GitHub will accept in bypass_actors
that the App is installed, and installed only on this repository
that any ruleset has been created, or is enforcing anything
_meta.those_remain: EXTERNAL / ADMIN REQUIRED. Confirm with: gh api /repos/nzebrian/eruofood-ai/installation --jq '{app_id, repository_selection, permissions}'

codeowners_deferred.reason: The repository has one human participant. Naming that person as the code owner of all seven roles would route every review back to the author, which GitHub forbids approving anyway — and for FINANCE it would read as four-eyes review on the money-moving paths while being none. Recording a release actor is a separate decision and does not require this one.
codeowners_deferred.consequence: .github/CODEOWNERS stays inert: every rule in it remains commented out and no review is routed to anybody.
codeowners_deferred.resolve_by: Grant a second real human write access, replace this block with a "codeowners" object naming them, and move ownership.json to MULTI_PERSON. Do not resolve it by naming the repository owner in every role, and do not name an assistant or a second account of the same person.

_release_actor_note.permissions: Contents: read and write; Metadata: read-only. No webhook, no events.
_release_actor_note.private_key: Held outside this repository. It is never committed, never printed, and never passed to a third-party action — the release-tag workflow signs its own JWT with openssl so the key stays in the runner's shell.
_release_actor_note.goes_where: rulesets[0].bypass_actors of production-tags-ruleset.json — the creation ruleset — and nowhere else. Never rulesets[1], whose bypass_actors must stay []. Authority to create a release tag is not authority to unmake one.
